sight translation is more difficult to perform than written translation.
sight translation and written translation have a different nature.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the oral and written translation processes within the PACTe translation competence model (PACTe, 2003).
the oral and written translation processes within the Translation Competence Model (TCM) developed by the PACTE group.
the analysis of the process of sight translation and written translation in order to verify empirically if the former can be considered as an interpreting modality, as some authors claim.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oral and written translation processes are very different.
the translation process is a complex process that is affected by many different factors.
the oral translation task is a more complex task than the written translation task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oral mode of translation is a different activity from the written mode of translation.

the translation competence model is an adequate framework to study translation processes and that the translation competence of translators is a multidimensional competence that includes cognitive, strategic and psychophysiological components.
sight translation is an activity which is very different from written translation, but which shares many of the features with consecutive and simultaneous interpreting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PACTE model of translation competence can benefit from the inclusion of oral translation as a source of data for the analysis of translation competence.
the oral translation task is a more challenging and complex activity for translators than the written translation task.
the translation process in sight translation and in written translation differs in terms of the strategies used and the types of problems encountered.
